extracted.intended_audience: Investigators applying to NIH R15/AREA grants (infectious diseases & microbiology) and NIH peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Summary statement and review criteria used by an NIH Special Emphasis Panel to evaluate an R15 (AREA) application, including criterion scores, strengths/weaknesses, and administrative determinations (human subjects, biohazards, budget, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (Impact Score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact: This summarizes reviewers' overall assessment of the likelihood that the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field. An impact/priority score is given (1-9) and averaged across voting reviewers then multiplied by 10 to yield the impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example text: 'Overall Impact: This innovative revised application aims to identify the metabolic pathways critical for Coxiella burnetii ... Enthusiasm for this revised application remained strong.' Scoring guidance (footnote): 'The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion of an application by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion assessing whether the project addresses an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field and the potential to improve scientific knowledge or clinical practice. Shown here as a numeric criterion score (example: 'Significance: 2').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer strengths/weaknesses examples provided: Strengths include pathogen importance (Coxiella burnetii causes significant morbidity/mortality; listed as a BSL3 select agent), potential applicability to other tick-borne pathogens, and potential to identify therapeutic targets. Weaknesses: 'None noted' in some critiques; in others the approach has been previously explored in other organisms (noted as a weakness). Use of concrete examples of significance (public health relevance, model for other pathogens) is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion assessing the investigator(s)'s qualifications, productivity, expertise, and ability to carry out the proposed work. Presented as a numeric score (example: 'Investigator(s): 1').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer evidence used includes publication record, relevant technical expertise (bioinformatics, high-throughput sequencing, microbiology), track record of mentoring, and collaborations/support letters. Typical strengths: 'accomplished young scientist', 'productive', 'necessary expertise'. Weaknesses: often 'None noted'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion assessing whether the application challenges and seeks to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel concepts, approaches, or methodologies. Shown as a numeric score (example: 'Innovation: 1' or '2').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of innovation from the application: hypothesis that critical metabolic pathways were acquired via horizontal gene transfer (HGT); use of a novel evolutionary genomics approach; tRNA-acquisition-based virulence mechanism. Weaknesses noted by reviewers include that genome-scale comparative approaches have been used in other organisms, or alternative evolutionary scenarios (e.g., environmental ancestor plus gene loss) that should be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion assessing the overall strategy, methodology, analyses, potential pitfalls, and whether the plans are well-reasoned and appropriate (presented as a numeric score, example: 'Approach: 1' or '2').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer guidance/examples: strengths included clearly described comparative genomic analysis, availability of a transposon-generated mutant library, RNA-seq validation, alternative methods described, and preliminary data supporting aims. Weaknesses included choice of specific tick Coxiella strain (other sequenced genomes might suffice), uncertainties about lab colony history, potential technical challenges (e.g., Tn mutagenesis lethality), and lack of clarity on methods for identifying HGT beyond taxonomic signals. Reviewers expect discussion of potential pitfalls and alternative approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion assessing the institutional support, equipment, and other physical resources available to the investigators (shown as numeric score, example: 'Environment: 2' or '1').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of evidence: collaborative shared research facility (PSU/OHSU/OSU), availability of Linux servers and core facilities, BSL-2 facilities/autoclave, access to collaborators, and reduced teaching load. Strengths listed as 'Excellent' with 'No concern.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether proposed research involving human subjects adequately protects their rights and welfare. In this application: 'Not Applicable (No Human Subjects)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, reviewers evaluate the human subjects protections; here the criterion is noted as not applicable. Applicants should explicitly state applicability and protections when human subjects are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether proposed research involving live vertebrate animals is justified and includes appropriate care and use. In this application: 'Not Applicable (No Vertebrate Animals)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, reviewers comment on animal welfare, justification, and appropriateness of models; applicants must provide details when vertebrate animals are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of any biohazardous materials or procedures and whether biosafety protections are adequate. In this application reviewers listed 'Biohazards: No concern' or 'Acceptable'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: BSL-2 containment for avirulent Nine Mile Phase II strain is noted; reviewers expect appropriate biosafety level justification and facilities. 'Acceptable' denotes no concerns about biohazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator whether the application is a resubmission and whether prior concerns were addressed. In this application: 'This is a revised application and the investigator addressed all of the prior concerns.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess whether the applicant responded appropriately to previous critiques; explicit statements about addressed concerns strengthen resubmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of work involving select agents and whether compliance and justifications are acceptable. In this application: 'Select Agents: Acceptable'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must disclose select agent status and provide required containment and compliance plans; reviewers note acceptability or issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of steps taken to authenticate key biological and chemical resources (e.g., cell lines, reagents). In this application: 'Acceptable' or 'Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources: Acceptable'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers expect a plan for authentication to ensure reproducibility; acceptable means the plan is sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans for data, model, and resource sharing (e.g., sequencing data), marked here as 'Acceptable'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH expects applicants to include resource sharing plans; reviewers note acceptability. When applicable, plans for sequence deposition, data access, and materials sharing should be described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of whether the requested budget and period of support are reasonable and appropriate. In this application: 'Recommend as Requested' and a Committee Budget Recommendation noting that the budget shown is the requested budget and may be adjusted by grants management staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee/Reviewer guidance: the budget may be recommended 'as requested' or adjusted; administrative notes explain that final costs will be calculated by institute grants management based on recommendations. Applicants should justify budget items and period of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee Administrative Notes / Next Steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative guidance and process notes provided by the Scientific Review Officer and committee (e.g., FOIA/redaction policy, next steps link, and how scores are handled).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from page: 'Text from the application is copyrighted... FOIA exemptions may apply and include substantial redactions.' 'Visit http://grants.nih.gov/grants/next_steps.htm.' Footnote explains score calculation and that criterion scores are submitted prior to meeting and not specifically discussed or calculated into the overall impact score. These procedural notes guide applicants on post-review handling and expectations.
